standard_prerequisites.name: Fibres of Spec(B) -> Spec(A) and the generic point, and the behaviour of the generic point under a flat injective map
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the geometry that lets case (7) be identified as the weakest hypothesis.

standard_prerequisites.name: Flat local homomorphisms are faithfully flat, so a flat map of domains is injective
standard_prerequisites.use: Guarantees that the generic point of Spec(B) maps to the generic point of Spec(A).

standard_prerequisites.name: The tensor product with the fraction field as a filtered colimit of localizations
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts the unit statement over B tensor_A K into a unit statement over some B_f, which is what produces the nonzero element of A cap J.

standard_prerequisites.name: No nontrivial specializations between fibre points for integral, quasi-finite, unramified and etale maps
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the remaining hypotheses to case (7).

core_obligations: Prove case (7): let K and L be the fraction fields of A and B; use the minimal-prime fact to see that the unique point of Spec(B) mapping to the generic point of Spec(A) is the generic point, so B tensor_A K has a unique prime with residue field L (proof lines 31721-31729).
Choose a nonzero b in J and note that b maps to a unit of L, hence to a unit of B tensor_A K (proof lines 31730-31732).

Use that B tensor_A K is the filtered colimit of the B_f over nonzero f in A to conclude that b maps to a unit of B_f for some nonzero f, so b b' = f^n with b' in B and n >= 1, whence f^n lies in A cap J (proof lines 31733-31736).

Show that assumptions (1) to (5) make A -> B flat, hence injective because flat local homomorphisms are faithfully flat, so the generic point of Spec(B) maps to the generic point of Spec(A) (proof lines 31740-31744).

Conclude (6) implies (7): if there are no nontrivial specializations between fibre points, the generic point of Spec(B) must be the unique point over the generic point of Spec(A) (proof lines 31744-31748).

Finish by establishing the absence of nontrivial specializations between fibre points in cases (1) to (5), using the integral case, the quasi-finite case, and that unramified and etale ring maps are quasi-finite (proof lines 31749-31759).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes domains A and B with a ring map A -> B satisfying at least one of seven listable properties (localization of an etale map; flat and localization of an unramified map; flat and localization of a quasi-finite map; flat and localization of an integral map; flat with no nontrivial specializations between fibre points; generic point to generic point with no such specializations; or exactly one point over the generic point), and concludes that A cap J is nonzero for every nonzero ideal J of B (source lines 31701-31718). The proof is organized around case (7), the weakest hypothesis. For case (7) it uses that the unique point of Spec(B) over the generic point is the generic point, so that B tensor_A K has a unique prime with residue field L; for a nonzero b in J, the image of b is a unit of L and hence of B tensor_A K, and since B tensor_A K is the filtered colimit of the B_f for nonzero f in A, b becomes a unit in some B_f, giving b b' = f^n and hence f^n in A cap J (proof lines 31721-31736). The rest of the proof is a careful reduction showing each of the other hypotheses implies (7): assumptions (1) to (5) make A -> B flat, hence injective because flat local homomorphisms are faithfully flat, so the generic point of Spec(B) maps to that of Spec(A); the absence of nontrivial specializations between fibre points then forces it to be the unique such point, so (6) implies (7); and finally the absence of such specializations is established for the integral, quasi-finite, unramified and etale cases by reference to the corresponding standard facts (proof lines 31739-31759). The non-routine content is the colimit-and-unit argument in case (7) together with the systematic reduction ladder from the other six hypotheses.
